correctness.rationale: Every same-side pair is at distance two; a cross-side nonedge has distance three and can use the omitted b_n,a_1 in that order. Thus the proposed set is feasible. A complement of size zero or one leaves a selected same-side pair with no omitted common neighbor. For a complement of size two, two omissions on one side are impossible for n>=4 by the same obstruction. For n=3 with B entirely selected, b_1 and b_2 force a_1 omitted and the one selected a_i has i>1, so its length-three path to b_1 cannot avoid an internal selected B-vertex; the reversed case is symmetric. If the omissions are a_p,b_q, the largest selected A index is at least n-1 and must be <=q, so q>1. Then b_1 is selected, and a same-side pair containing b_1 forces p=1. Now a_n remains selected, forcing q=n. For the K_{n,n} comparison every choice of one omission from each side works and no same-side double omission works when n>=3, giving n^2. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/checks/1.py enumerates masks of all geodesic interiors and all complements of size at most two for n=2..14; it finds six size-two maxima for n=2 and just the claimed maximum for each n=3..14. This finite oracle is corroborative only.
